title: A Map, One Step at a Time
summary: Two colleagues talk through how a navigator helps a family understand Minnesota disability services, from the first stack of papers to the letters that come after services start.
learningObjective: Two colleagues talk through how a navigator helps a family understand Minnesota disability services, from the first stack of papers to the letters that come after services start.

sources.title: Minnesota Department of Human Services — MnCHOICES
Minnesota Statutes 2025, section 256B.4905 — Home and Community-Based Services Policy Statement

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: A parent hands a navigator a stack of papers and says, I don't know what any of this is. Where do you start?

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Not with all of it, I hope.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: Right. Find the one paper that matters now, explain it and write down the next step. The whole path has five parts: first contact, assessment, planning and choice, services starting, and renewals and changes. But a family only needs the next step today.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Who does the assessment in Minnesota?

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: Lead agencies: counties, tribal nations and managed care organizations, using the state's MnCHOICES system and certified assessors. A navigator doesn't assess. A navigator helps the family get ready.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Some families want to show they're doing fine, so nobody thinks they can't cope.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: That's very human. The navigator can explain that the assessment is how the agency learns what help might make life easier, and talk through a real week with them, hard nights included. Then the family decides what to share, in their own words. Preparing, never scripting.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Then they get a list of providers and a deadline.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: And this is where the law helps. For people on waivers, Minnesota's informed decision-making process includes things like all available options, cultural needs, visits or hands-on experiences, talking with peers and enough time to decide. A family who knows they can ask for a visit is in a much stronger position.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: And once services are approved, it's done?

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: Not quite. That's when things quietly stall. Help the family know what should happen next, follow up with the case manager when they agree, read every letter together for dates and appeal rights, and keep a simple record.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: And free help along the way?

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: Disability Hub MN is a free statewide resource. For health coverage, MNsure navigators help for free too. A navigator doesn't have to know everything. They have to know where to go.
